es: Describir datos con proporciones y comparaciones precisas (the vast majority, a sizeable minority, just under a third, twice as many, account for, outnumber) y leer con sentido crítico lo que una cifra sugiere.

teaching.en: Roughly a third of the residents, 34 per cent, use the bus daily, yet the vast majority, 91 per cent, own a bicycle.
teaching.es: Aproximadamente un tercio de los vecinos, el 34 por ciento, usa el autobús a diario, pero la gran mayoría, el 91 por ciento, tiene una bicicleta.
teaching.explanationEs: Roughly suaviza la cifra; the vast majority equivale a «casi todos»; per cent no lleva -s.
segments: Roughly a third of the residents, 34 per cent, use the bus
daily, yet the vast majority, 91 per cent, own a bicycle.
teaching.audioText: Roughly a third of the residents, 34 per cent, use the bus daily, yet the vast majority, 91 per cent, own a bicycle.

teaching.en: Cyclists now outnumber train passengers: twice as many residents cycle as take the train, although a sizeable minority still drive.
teaching.es: Los ciclistas ya superan en número a los pasajeros del tren: el doble de vecinos usa la bicicleta que el tren, aunque una minoría considerable sigue conduciendo.
teaching.explanationEs: Outnumber es transitivo (outnumber someone, sin preposición); twice as many… as compara dos cantidades contables.
segments: Cyclists now outnumber train passengers: twice as many residents cycle
as take the train, although a sizeable minority still drive.
teaching.audioText: Cyclists now outnumber train passengers: twice as many residents cycle as take the train, although a sizeable minority still drive.

teaching.en: A negligible proportion, barely two per cent, arrive by taxi, so the council can safely ignore that figure.
teaching.es: Una proporción insignificante, apenas el dos por ciento, llega en taxi, así que el municipio puede ignorar esa cifra sin riesgo.
teaching.explanationEs: Barely y a negligible proportion subrayan que una cantidad es tan pequeña que casi no cuenta.
segments: A negligible proportion, barely two per cent, arrive by
taxi, so the council can safely ignore that figure.
teaching.audioText: A negligible proportion, barely two per cent, arrive by taxi, so the council can safely ignore that figure.

teaching.en: Car use rose slightly, from just under a fifth of journeys to just over a fifth, which is hardly a trend.
teaching.es: El uso del auto subió ligeramente, de un poco menos de un quinto de los viajes a un poco más de un quinto, lo que difícilmente es una tendencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Just under / just over sitúan la cifra respecto a una fracción redonda; slightly acompaña cambios pequeños.
segments: Car use rose slightly, from just under a fifth of journeys
to just over a fifth, which is hardly a trend.
teaching.audioText: Car use rose slightly, from just under a fifth of journeys to just over a fifth, which is hardly a trend.

teaching.en: Students account for roughly half of all cyclists, so any change to the cycle lanes will affect them most.
teaching.es: Los estudiantes representan aproximadamente la mitad de todos los ciclistas, así que cualquier cambio en los carriles bici les afectará más.
teaching.explanationEs: Account for + porcentaje indica qué parte del total supone un grupo; no se traduce como «dar cuenta de».
segments: Students account for roughly half of all cyclists, so any
change to the cycle lanes will affect them most.
teaching.audioText: Students account for roughly half of all cyclists, so any change to the cycle lanes will affect them most.

prompt.es: Elige la expresión que describe fielmente el dato del gráfico.

choices.text: a sizeable minority of the students
a negligible proportion of the students
the vast majority of the students

feedback.es: Siete de doscientos es una cantidad tan pequeña que casi no cuenta: a negligible proportion.

hint.es: Fíjate en que 3,5 por ciento es una cifra muy baja.

origin.text: Chart: of 200 students, 7 arrive by taxi, which is 3.5 per cent of the group.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los estudiantes representan aproximadamente la mitad de los ciclistas.»

feedback.es: Account for + porcentaje expresa qué parte del total supone un grupo.

hint.es: El verbo va seguido de for y significa «representar una parte».

origin.text: Figures from the cycle scheme show that students ___ for roughly half of all cyclists; staff make up most of the rest.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con el porcentaje al que suele corresponder.

feedback.es: Cada expresión cubre una franja distinta: casi todos, casi la mitad, una parte notable y casi nada.

hint.es: Ordénalas mentalmente de la mayor a la menor proporción.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué advierten los autores sobre el aumento del ciclismo.

choices.text: That cycling is growing too slowly to matter to the council.
That the fall in car use is the real story here.
That the growth is striking, but the numbers involved remain very small.

feedback.es: Los autores piden cautela: duplicar un dato muy pequeño llama la atención, pero los conductores siguen siendo diez veces más; ni restan importancia al ciclismo ni ven en la bajada del auto la noticia.

origin.audio: The council's latest figures show that car journeys have fallen slightly, from 41 to 40 per cent, whereas cycling has doubled, from two to four per cent. Even so, drivers still outnumber cyclists ten to one, and the authors warn against reading too much into a change this small.

prompt.es: Completa: «La proporción de conductores bajó ligeramente este año.»

feedback.es: Un punto porcentual es un cambio pequeño: slightly acompaña verbos como fell o rose.

origin.text: The proportion of people who drive fell ___ this year, from 41 to 40 per cent, a change too small to be called a trend.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe fielmente los datos.

choices.text: Walkers account for just under half of the pupils.
Cyclists account for roughly a third of the pupils.
Bus users outnumber cyclists by a wide margin.

feedback.es: 245 de 500 es un poco menos de la mitad; los ciclistas son una cuarta parte y los usuarios del autobús no superan a los ciclistas.

origin.text: Survey of 500 pupils: 245 walk, 130 cycle and 125 take the bus.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere el informe sobre la petición de un estacionamiento nuevo?

choices.text: It reflects the wishes of the drivers, who are the largest group.
It is a minor concern for staff compared with bicycle storage.
It matters more to drivers who live close to the site.

feedback.es: Solo una proporción insignificante lo pidió, mientras que casi todos los menores de treinta pidieron guardabicicletas; además, los conductores (360 de 1.200) no son el grupo mayoritario.

origin.text: Commuting report. The survey was sent to every member of staff, and replies came back from all three sites. Of the 1,200 employees who answered, 780 use public transport, 360 drive and 60 cycle. Among the drivers, just over half live within ten kilometres of the site, so a tram stop would suit them. Cyclists are barely five per cent of the total, yet nearly everyone under thirty asked for secure bicycle storage. Women account for roughly 58 per cent of respondents but only a third of the drivers. Only a negligible proportion of staff asked for a new car park, although several admitted that they seldom use the present one.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las mujeres superan en número a los hombres en doscientas personas.»

feedback.es: Outnumber es un verbo transitivo: se construye sin preposición y significa ser más numerosos que otro grupo.

origin.text: Of the 1,200 respondents, 700 were women and 500 were men, so women ___ men by two hundred.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué Mia menciona que solo contestaron cincuenta personas.

choices.text: She suspected the survey had been sent to the wrong staff.
She thought forty per cent was too low to be worth reporting.
The percentage sounded much bigger than the small numbers justified.

feedback.es: Mia señala que un cuarenta por ciento son solo veinte personas: el porcentaje suena más grande de lo que justifican los números.

origin.audio: In Monday's meeting, Tom presented the figures from the staff survey. Forty per cent of employees, he said, were unhappy with the parking, but when Mia looked at the table she noticed that only fifty people had answered, so forty per cent meant twenty people. Tom agreed that a percentage can sound dramatic when the sample is small, and he promised to add the real numbers to the report.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aproximadamente dos tercios de los encuestados viven a menos de diez minutos.»

answer.text: Roughly two thirds of the respondents live within ten minutes

feedback.es: Roughly suaviza la fracción y within ten minutes cierra el dato con la distancia.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura adopta el autor ante el verbo «surged»?

choices.text: He finds it too dramatic for such small numbers.
He thinks it plays down a real and striking rise.
He uses it because the percentage has doubled.

feedback.es: El autor reconoce que el dato se duplicó, pero considera que el verbo exagera lo que los números pequeños permiten afirmar.

origin.text: Headline writers love dramatic verbs. A rise from two to four per cent is a doubling, yet it still describes only a small share of the population, and to say that cycling has surged is to let the verb do the work that the numbers have not earned.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ese 29 % queda un poco por debajo de un tercio.»

feedback.es: Just under sitúa la cifra justo por debajo de una fracción redonda: 29 es un poco menos de un tercio.

origin.text: In the vote, 29 per cent of residents took part. That is ___ a third, so nobody can claim that the neighbourhood as a whole has spoken.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué implica la precaución de los autores.

choices.text: Most pupils are afraid of cycling near the school.
Safety may look better than other pupils would report.
Three quarters of all pupils cycle to school.

feedback.es: Como solo respondieron quienes ya van en bicicleta, el dato puede hacer que la seguridad parezca mayor de lo que dirían los demás.

origin.audio: Three out of four pupils who answered said that they felt safe cycling to school. But the survey was sent only to pupils who already cycle, so the authors caution that the figure tells us little about everyone else.
